q: The DICGC Act is related to which sector?
explain: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation Act deals with insurance of bank deposits and credit guarantee, so it concerns banking.

q: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation Act was passed in which year?
explain: The Act dates from 1961; the Corporation itself was formed in 1978 when DIC and CGCI merged.

q: Where is the headquarters of DICGC?
explain: DICGC’s head office is in Mumbai.

q: The authorised capital of DICGC is ₹50 crore, fully issued and subscribed by whom?
explain: DICGC is a wholly owned subsidiary of the RBI, which subscribes its entire capital.

q: The insurance cover of DICGC per depositor is currently limited to:
explain: The cover was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh in February 2020.

q: Premium for deposit insurance is to be remitted by the insured bank not later than the last day of May and which other month each year?
explain: Premium is paid half-yearly, by the end of May and the end of November.

q: The concept of insuring deposits kept with banks first received attention in 1948 after a banking crisis in which region?
explain: The crisis in Bengal in 1948 brought the idea of deposit insurance into focus.

q: Which committee supported the insuring of banking deposits in 1950?
explain: The Rural Banking Enquiry Committee supported deposit insurance in 1950.

q: What does the insurance cover under DICGC include?
options: Principal and interest only for the first three months
explain: The ₹5 lakh limit takes in principal plus interest.

q: Who pays the deposit insurance premium to DICGC?
explain: The premium is paid by the insured bank and cannot be passed on to depositors.

q: DICGC was formed by merging which two bodies?
options: Deposit Insurance Corporation and Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Ltd.
explain: DIC and CGCI were merged on 15 July 1978 to integrate deposit insurance and credit guarantee.

q: On which date was DICGC established?
explain: 15 July 1978 is the formation date; 1 January 1962 is when the 1961 Act came into force, and 14 January 1971 is when CGCI was promoted.

q: When was the Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Ltd. (CGCI) promoted by the RBI?
explain: CGCI was promoted as a public limited company on 14 January 1971.

q: The failure of which banks in 1960 made the RBI and the Government think seriously about deposit insurance?
options: Palai Central Bank and Laxmi Bank
Global Trust Bank and Lakshmi Vilas Bank
Bank of Baroda and Bank of India
Bank of Bengal and Imperial Bank
explain: The crash of the Palai Central Bank Ltd. and the Laxmi Bank Ltd. in 1960 triggered serious action.

q: When did the Deposit Insurance Act, 1961 come into force?
explain: The Bill was introduced on 21 August 1961 and received assent on 7 December 1961, but the Act began on 1 January 1962.

q: What was the original insurance cover per depositor under Section 16(1) of the DICGC Act?
explain: The initial cover was ₹1,500 and was later enhanced several times.

q: The deposit insurance limit was raised to ₹30,000 with effect from:
explain: ₹20,000 applied from 1976, ₹30,000 from July 1980 and ₹1 lakh from May 1993.

q: The deposit insurance limit was raised from ₹30,000 to ₹1 lakh in:
explain: The limit became ₹1,00,000 with effect from 1 May 1993.

q: The deposit insurance limit was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh in:
explain: The cover was raised as per the budget provision, effective 4 February 2020.

q: Which committee had recommended a five-time increase in the deposit insurance cap to ₹5 lakh?
options: Damodaran Committee on Customer Services in Banks
explain: The 2011 Damodaran Committee asked for a five-time increase because incomes and deposit sizes had grown.

q: The demand for increasing the insurance limit to ₹5 lakh became stronger after the collapse of which bank?
explain: The PMC Bank collapse strengthened the demand for a higher cover.

q: What is the deposit insurance limit in 1976?
Which of the following deposits is NOT covered under DICGC insurance?
explain: Inter-bank deposits are excluded; savings, fixed, current and recurring deposits are covered.

q: Which of these deposits is excluded from DICGC cover?
options: Deposits of Central and State Governments
explain: Government deposits are not insured. Current accounts and ordinary customers’ deposits are.

q: Which type of deposit is covered by DICGC?
explain: Recurring deposits are insured; the other three types are excluded.

q: Which of the following is covered by the Deposit Insurance Scheme of DICGC?
options: Co-operative banks as defined in Section 2(gg) of the DICGC Act
explain: Eligible co-operative banks are covered; primary co-operative societies are not insured.

q: Which of the following is NOT insured by DICGC?
options: Branches of foreign banks in India
explain: Primary co-operative societies are outside the scheme, while RRBs, LABs and foreign bank branches are included.

q: As per the book, DICGC charges a premium of how much on deposits held by a bank?
explain: As per the book the rate is 10 paise per ₹100 of deposits; the rate has since been revised upward, so check the latest figure.

q: A bank can lose its DICGC registration if it fails to pay premium for how many consecutive half-year periods?
explain: The Corporation can cancel registration after three consecutive half-years of non-payment.

q: Under which condition can DICGC restore the registration of a de-registered bank?
options: The bank requests it and pays all premium due with interest
The RBI Governor passes an order
The bank pays only the latest premium
explain: Restoration needs a request from the bank and payment of all dues from the date of default with interest.

q: Who is the Chairman of the Board of Directors of DICGC?
options: A Deputy Governor of the RBI
explain: A Deputy Governor of the RBI chairs the Board.

q: How many departments does DICGC have?
explain: The four departments are Accounts, Deposit Insurance, Credit Guarantee and Administration.

q: Which fund of DICGC is used for meeting establishment and administrative expenses?
explain: The General Fund pays for establishment and administration; the other two settle claims.

q: The Credit Guarantee Fund of DICGC is funded by:
explain: The Deposit Insurance Fund is fed by premium; the Credit Guarantee Fund by guarantee fees.

q: Deposit insurance was initially extended to which category of banks?
options: Only the State Bank of India
explain: The scheme began with functioning commercial banks, including SBI and its subsidiaries and foreign bank branches.

q: The insurance cover is calculated for deposits held in the same right and capacity in:
options: All branches of the bank taken together
All banks in the country combined
explain: The cover applies per depositor per bank across all its branches together.
